signals.title: tests/contracts/validate.sh dies silently under `set -euo pipefail` when a prose-drift grep finds nothing, so `make verify` fails with zero diagnostic output.
signals.repro: Rename or renumber a step heading the validator greps for (e.g. change prep's `5. **Cut the branch**` to `6.`), then run `bash tests/contracts/validate.sh`. Exit code is 1 and nothing is printed — not even the script's own `die` message.
signals.evidence: validate.sh:26-28 assigns via a pipeline: `prep_branch_line="$(grep -n '...' file | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)"`. With `set -euo pipefail` (line 4) a no-match grep fails the pipeline, so the assignment itself aborts the script before control ever reaches the `|| die "prep must cut the branch before seeding human gates"` on line 31. `bash -x` trace ends at `+ prep_branch_line=` with no further output. The same construct is used for `prep_seed_line`. Fix: append `|| true` to the command substitution (or use a `grep ... || echo` fallback) so the intended die message actually prints. Found while diagnosing a red gate in sprint `discover-judgment`, where the missing message turned a one-line regex fix into a bash -x investigation.
